headline: AI Agent Development Services in 2026
description: What AI agents are in 2026, single vs multi-agent systems, the agent tech stack, guardrails, how to evaluate them, costs, and use cases by industry.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?

acceptedAnswer.text: A chatbot responds to a message in one turn. An agent runs a multi-step loop, calling real tools and using live data to complete a goal autonomously. The engineering effort is in the tools, guardrails and evaluation, not the prompt.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build an AI agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused single-domain agent with a handful of tools, a proper evaluation set and a human review step typically takes 4-8 weeks. Multi-agent systems, heavy integration surface or strict compliance extend that.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a multi-agent system?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. A single well-scoped agent handles most production use cases at lower cost and latency. Add more agents only when a problem clearly decomposes into independent specialities and you've proven the simpler version.

mainEntity.name: How do you control AI agent costs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Token spend scales with context size and loop count, so we use retrieval instead of stuffing context, prompt caching, a right-sized model per task, and hard caps on iterations and spend.

mainEntity.name: How do you stop an agent doing something harmful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Least-privilege tools, human approval for irreversible actions, loop and cost caps, prompt-injection defences and sandboxed execution, plus an evaluation suite that catches regressions before production.
